blocks.heading: Premise
blocks.text: Tulsa's The Meridian Museum of Art & World Cultures is unveiling Treasures of the World, a lavish exhibition drawn largely from the private collection of controversial billionaire donor Sterling Voss. The centerpiece is the fictional thirteenth-century Isfahan Star Bowl, a silver-inlaid brass basin whose incomplete provenance has already attracted quiet controversy. Sterling remains offstage during Act I. Just as guests finish exploring the exhibition and begin dinner, he is found dead in the Donor Salon. He has been poisoned. One of the guests did it - but that guest only learns their role when the murderer animal is announced.

blocks.heading: How the game works
bullets: 15 core roles, 10 secondary roles, 5 tertiary roles; tier labels are never shown to players.
2.5 hours of active game inside a roughly 6:00-9:30 PM evening with buffet dinner.
Act I is movement-heavy; Acts II-III prioritize roleplay and social deduction.
No phones or QR codes. All mechanics are physical.
Almost no mandatory read-aloud until the final confessions.
Medium deduction difficulty: the killer should be discoverable but not obvious.
The facilitator may play a full character and does not know who the murderer is.

blocks.heading: Player truth rules
bullets: Innocent players may evade, omit, deflect, and protect private information, but may not invent false factual events.
The murderer may lie as needed.
If a card explicitly instructs a player to reveal or submit evidence, they must do so.
Players may share discoveries from Act I freely. Encourage conversation rather than hoarding.

blocks.text: Prepare two identical sets of 15 easy animal names. Core players draw from Player Bowl A as they arrive and memorize their animal. After all core attendees have drawn, look at the unused slips left in Bowl A and remove those same animals from Murderer Bowl B. Shuffle Bowl B and draw one card. You now know the murderer animal but still do not know who drew it. After Sterling's death is announced, say: “If your animal is ___, follow the MURDERER column in your packet. Everyone else follows INNOCENT.” Optional-role guests can draw from a separate set of non-murderer animals if you want everyone to participate in the ritual.

blocks.heading: Murder announcement / Read aloud
blocks.text: “Before Sterling Voss could enter Founders Hall for his remarks, he was found collapsed in the Donor Salon. The museum's physician has confirmed that this was not a natural death. Sterling Voss was poisoned. From this point on, the gala is an investigation. If your animal is [MURDERER ANIMAL], follow the MURDERER instructions in your packet. Everyone else follows INNOCENT. Do not announce which column you are reading.”

blocks.heading: Release the fixed evidence
blocks.text: The separate clue/forensics print pack contains five cards labeled F1-F5. Keep them face down until Act III, then place all five on the Evidence Table. You do not need to know their contents in advance.

title: Turn the house into a museum

table: Founders Hall - main gala floor, ballots, evidence table, dinner seating
Grand Gallery - centerpiece display and contemporary works
Sculpture Court - buffet and hospitality zone
Conservation Lab - condition reports and one scavenger clue
Moving Image Gallery / Archives - press and audiovisual materials
Silk Road Gallery - world cultures display
Powder Room / Patron Lounge - one discreet clue, no essential evidence
Donor Salon - fictional murder scene; guests may enter only during Act I scavenger hunt

blocks.text: Sixteen numbered clues are hidden around the museum. A finder earns one point and brings the clue to the Evidence Table, where it becomes public. No required order or checklist. End the hunt when time is called; missing finds cannot make the murder unsolvable.

table: Near the mirror or folded hand towel
Behind a frame or display card
Near the room sign or faux security note
Beside an art label or sketch
Attached to or inside a prop crate/box

blocks.heading: Ballots & the reveal
bullets: Each ballot names one murderer, one piece of evidence, and a motive; plus Best Actor and Best Costume.
Tally murderer votes first. Announce the three most-accused characters in ascending order.
Those three read their FINAL STATEMENT from the appropriate Innocent/Murderer branch.
If the actual murderer is not among the top three, award the murderer an 'Escaped Justice' prize, then ask the murderer animal to identify themselves and read the confession.
Award scavenger recognition separately so solving the murder is not the only way to win.

title: Preparation / This week & the day before

blocks.heading: This week
bullets: Assign the 15 core roles first; add secondary and tertiary roles as RSVPs grow.
Send each guest only their spoiler-safe pre-party character sheet plus the invitation.
Tell guests costumes can be assembled from normal formalwear plus one character-specific element.

blocks.heading: Day before
bullets: Print this guide, props, private player packets, and randomized A/B evidence cards.
Without reading the secret material, place each character's private page plus both A/B evidence cards in a labeled envelope.
Cut two identical sets of core animal cards for Player Bowl A and Murderer Bowl B.
Cut ballots and scavenger clues; prepare an Evidence Table and scavenger score sheet.
Stage inexpensive exhibit objects and placards in the room map.

blocks.heading: Print settings
blocks.text: Print single-sided at Actual size (100%). Print private files face down and keep the output tray covered. Follow the separate host-safe assembly guide to cut and seal packets. Each guest receives two private pages plus both A/B evidence cards.

blocks.heading: 1–2 hours before arrival
bullets: Hide the sixteen Act I clues. Do not make them extremely difficult; movement and discovery matter more than searching skill.
Place the fixed forensic cards face down for Act III.
Put each attending player's private packet at their assigned dining seat or hand it to them at check-in.

Start with all 15 core animals in both bowls. After the attending core players have drawn from Bowl A, note the unused animal slips still left there, remove those same names from Murderer Bowl B, then draw the murderer animal from Bowl B.
Set out awards, pens, ballots, and a container for submitted Evidence Update cards.

blocks.heading: Check the envelopes
blocks.text: One labeled envelope per attending guest: two private packet pages and both A/B evidence cards. Keep all contents private until the indicated act.

blocks.heading: Check the bowls
blocks.text: Two identical sets of core animal slips. Optional animals belong in a separate bowl. Remove each absent core animal from Bowl B before drawing the murderer animal.
Facilitator logistics only: assign all 15 core roles first. Add secondary roles next, then tertiary roles. Do not show tier labels to guests.

blocks.heading: Protect your own experience
blocks.text: The secret player packets contain each character's relationship to Sterling, hidden complication, innocent branch, murderer branch, evidence-card instructions, and final statements. To preserve your own experience, print those files without reading them and seal each character's packet. The Facilitator Guide contains everything you need to run the night without knowing which branch anyone activates.
